page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Set up integration by parts
lines: Take first function u = logx, second v = 1/x²
steps.why: logx must be the first function u in ILATE order, since it has no simple antiderivative of its own — x⁻² is integrated instead, giving v=−1/x.
common_mistakes: Taking u=1/x² and v=logx the wrong way round, which needs ∫logx dx — itself a by-parts integral, doubling the work.
steps.memory_tip: logx is ALWAYS u in a by-parts split — it has no antiderivative that helps, so it can never be the part you integrate.

steps.label: Apply the by-parts rule for the final answer
steps.why: The by-parts rule u·v − ∫v·(du) leaves a plain ∫dx/x² = −1/x to finish, giving both terms in the final answer their own negative sign.
common_mistakes: Sign slip on the second integral: ∫(−1/x)(1/x)dx = −∫dx/x², and ∫dx/x²=−1/x, so the two minus signs combine to give +∫dx/x², then integrate to −1/x — lose that sign and the final answer comes out as −logx/x + 1/x + c instead of the correct −logx/x − 1/x + c.
steps.memory_tip: Two separate minus signs appear in this by-parts working — track them one at a time rather than guessing the final sign.
